title: Semiconductor Absolute Maximum Ratings
gist: A SemiWiki forum post argues that when process migration silently degrades a part's Absolute Maximum Ratings, the part number should change. The concrete case: a major supplier of the NE5532 dual op-amp cut its Absolute Maximum Operating Voltage from the historic 44VDC to 36VDC while keeping the same commercial part number, creating latent failure risk in legacy professional-audio designs that run at 40-42VDC.

insights.claim: Improved semiconductor processing and manufacturing does not uniformly improve device specifications; for analog integrated circuits, newer processes can degrade specific performance parameters.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Analog franchises cannot be modeled as monotonically improving with node migration — shrinking a legacy analog part can destroy the very headroom that made it valuable.
insights.quote: Certainly with improved processing and manufacturing, certain processes impact perfomance specifications-in particular for analog integrated circuits.
insights.locator: Certainly with improved processing and manufacturing

insights.claim: A part's datasheet contains two distinct specification classes — performance parameters and Absolute Maximum Ratings — and the latter defines the survivable operating envelope rather than typical behavior.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Reliability exposure in a bill of materials lives in the AbsMax column, not the performance column, so spec-sheet diffing must track both separately.
insights.quote: Part number specifications generally define the performance parameters and Absolute Maximum Ratings.

insights.claim: The voltage reduction on the part in question is attributed directly to new process technology rather than to a marketing or derating decision.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Once a legacy analog die is moved to a newer process, the voltage rollback is structural and irreversible for that supplier — second-sourcing, not a supplier fix, is the remedy.
insights.quote: New processes of course result in the lower voltage.

insights.claim: The NE5532 dual operational amplifier was developed by Signetics around 1979 and was adopted largely for its low noise and its high Absolute Maximum Operating Voltage of 44VDC.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: A ~47-year-old analog part still shipping into production shows how sticky legacy analog sockets are — and how much installed base is exposed when its spec moves.
insights.quote: This part, developed by Signetics around 1979 and well accepted due to its low noise and high Absolute Maximun Operating Voltage of 44VDC.
insights.locator: This part, developed by Signetics around 1979

insights.claim: One major supplier, among several sources of the part, has recently cut the maximum operating voltage specification from 44VDC to 36VDC.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: An 8V cut on a multi-sourced commodity part means supplier identity now determines whether a nominally interchangeable component is safe in a given design.
insights.quote: Recently, a major manufacturer (one of several suppliers) of this part has reduced the Maximum Operating Voltage to 36VDC.

insights.claim: The part has been a mainstay of professional audio equipment, with designs from vendors such as Otari and Audio Designs operating it at 40 to 42VDC.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Legacy rail voltages of 40-42VDC sit above the new 36VDC ceiling, so the downgraded part is out of spec in exactly the installed base that consumes it.
insights.quote: It has been a mainstay in professional audio since then - in many cases operating at 40 to 42 VDC (reference Otari, Audio Designs and others).
insights.locator: It has been a mainstay in professional audio

themes.theme: Part numbering as a reliability control

insights.claim: A reduction in a part's Absolute Maximum Operating Voltage should force issuance of a new part number, because the industry already uses distinct part numbers to distinguish voltage variants such as 5V and 3.3V versions within the same family.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Existing industry convention already supports voltage-keyed part numbers, so keeping the old number for a downgraded die is a controllable process failure, not a technical necessity.
insights.quote: Of course many part families may have a 5V and 3.3V etc versions, but these have unique part numbers to define this critical parameter.
insights.locator: Of course many part families may have a 5V

insights.claim: Procurement practice is the transmission mechanism for the risk: many purchasing agents order against the commercial part number alone and do not read the specification sheets.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Silent spec changes bypass every buyer-side control when the part number is the only key, which makes supply-chain component-qualification tooling a real unmet need.
insights.quote: many Purchasing Agents do not read the spec sheets - they use only the commercial part number.

insights.claim: Installing the reduced-AbsMax version of the part into an existing design is expected to produce failures and other undesirable outcomes.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: Field-failure and warranty exposure can be created downstream by an upstream process change no one flagged — a latent liability that never appears in a supplier's own reliability data.
insights.quote: If this reduced AbsMax part is installed in a existing design, likely failure and other undesirable results could occur.
insights.locator: If this reduced AbsMax part is installed

insights.claim: The part is unlikely to be designed into new products because higher performance alternatives now exist, yet it will remain available in the market for some time.
insights.speaker: TomCee
insights.so_what: The revenue tail of obsolete analog parts is repair and replacement demand, precisely the channel where a silent spec downgrade does the most damage.
insights.quote: Further, there are higher performance parts and this part would not necessarily be implemented in new designs.
insights.locator: Further, there are higher performance parts
